text:
agent1 (pricing) here. pricing.py is done. API (all money in float dollars, percentages as fractions, misses return None):
- get_item(sku) -> {'sku','name','price','category'} or None
- get_item_price(sku) -> float or None
- list_items() -> list of item dicts (catalog order)
- get_customer(customer_id) -> {'id','name','discount','region'} or None
- get_discount(customer_id) -> fraction (C1 -> 0.10) or None
- list_customers() -> list of customer dicts
Returned dicts are copies. Data is read from data_pricing/ relative to pricing.py. Tell me if you need a different shape, e.g. a line-item helper.

agent3 (invoice) here. Proposed interface (also in agreement_log INTERFACE topic). pricing.py (agent1): is_known_sku(sku)->bool; unit_price(sku)->Decimal dollars (Decimal('0') if unknown); customer_discount(customer_id)->Decimal multiplier (10% off = Decimal('0.90'); unknown customer = Decimal('1')); customer_name(customer_id)->str ('' if unknown). tax.py (agent2): tax_for(customer_id, lines, discount_multiplier)->(tax_amount Decimal dollars rounded to cent half-up, rate Decimal multiplier e.g. Decimal('1.0825')); lines = list of (sku, line_amount Decimal before discount) for known skus only, in order; unknown customer -> (Decimal('0.00'), Decimal('1')). agent2: if you need the discount applied differently to taxable base, tell me; tax rules stay in tax.py. Please reply accept/object or propose changes.

agent2 (tax.py) is done. Proposed API, so invoice/pricing can align:
- tax.calculate_tax(region, lines, discount_pct) -> int cents.
  region: customer's region code (e.g. 'TX'), or None for an unknown customer (tax 0).
  lines: iterable of (category, line_amount_cents) pairs.
  discount_pct: customer's discount in percent (e.g. 10).
  Raises KeyError if the region is not in rates.csv. Rounds half up to the cent.
- Also: tax.tax_pct_for_region(region) -> Decimal, tax.is_exempt(category) -> bool.
pricing should supply each customer's region and discount_pct; invoice passes order lines as (category, amount_cents). Object if you need a different shape.

agent3: agent2, your API differs from my v1 (cents ints, region-based, discount_pct passed in). To avoid two competing proposals I will accept YOUR tax shape: tax.calculate_tax(region, lines, discount_pct) -> int cents, lines = (category, line_amount_cents) list, region None for unknown customer. I will convert money at my boundary (Decimal dollars internally in invoice.py). I need from tax: a percent for display; I will call tax.tax_pct_for_region(region) -> Decimal (e.g. Decimal('8.25')) and treat None region as 0. Please confirm tax_pct_for_region returns percent (8.25), not multiplier. agent1: please confirm pricing will provide: item lookup by sku -> (category, unit price in cents or Decimal dollars; tell me which), customer -> (region, discount_pct) with defaults for unknown (region None, discount_pct 0), and customer display name or I show the id. Reply here; I will build against these until objections.

agent3: thanks both. I will adapt at my boundary to what you actually shipped, so no more API changes needed from you. invoice.py will call: agent1 pricing: get_item(sku) (None -> UNKNOWN SKU; uses 'price' float dollars and 'category'), get_customer(id) (None -> unknown; uses 'name', 'discount' fraction, 'region'). agent2 tax: calculate_tax(region, [(category, line_cents)], discount_pct) with discount_pct = percent (e.g. 10), region None for unknown customer; tax_pct_for_region(region) for the displayed percent. agent2: please confirm tax_pct_for_region returns percent (8.25), not fraction (0.0825). Also: calculate_tax should apply the discount to the taxable base itself (the spec example needs tax on A only after 10% off: 1.86). I convert floats with Decimal(str(x)). agent1: please make sure unit price in data is 2 decimals so str(float) is exact.
